A1.justification: Both PDFs describe ActAlign and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables and appendices. Corresponding content can be matched reliably despite the journal reformatting and additional material in v3.

before.justification: V2 reports original ActionAtlas classification experiments, component and prompting ablations, and qualitative alignment analyses, including smoothing results in Appendix A.

after.justification: V3 retains those original experiments and adds pooling comparisons, sub-action order perturbations, domain-level results and another qualitative alignment example.

M1.justification: The GPT-4o scripts, context augmentation, frozen SigLIP encoders, smoothing, sigmoid affinities and normalized DTW classification remain unchanged. Clarifications about metadata and pretrained scaling parameters document the existing procedure rather than establish a method revision.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same ActionAtlas coverage: 898 videos, 558 actions and 56 sports domains. V3's four-domain breakdown and rodeo example analyze retained coverage rather than introduce another dataset or task.

E2.justification: All Table 1 comparators remain. V3 Table 3 adds context-augmented class-name SigLIP and a Bag-of-Words variant that mean-pools sub-action representations, extending comparisons within the existing backbone family.

E3.justification: V3 introduces controlled evaluations that reverse or permute the ten-step short-fixed scripts and separately evaluate the four largest domains. The original candidate sets, Top-k metrics, backbone and smoothing setting remain. Appendix H newly documents existing VLM conditions rather than establishes that those evaluations changed.

E4.justification: V3 substantially broadens validation with controls separating language enrichment from temporal alignment, order-sensitivity tests in Tables 3–4, domain stratification in Table 10, and a rodeo alignment case in Figure 9/Table 11. The original component, prompting, smoothing and failure analyses are retained.

E5.justification: V3 adds uncertainty reporting for ActAlign's main Top-1 result, 30.40±0.11, and reports five randomized-order trials with ± values for all three accuracies in Table 4. V2 gave ActAlign point estimates. The main result's run count and meaning of ± remain unspecified.

E6.justification: New control, order, domain and qualitative results materially expand the evidence. V3 Table 3 reports 28.51% and 29.06% Top-1 for context-augmented and Bag-of-Words SigLIP versus ActAlign's 30.29%; Table 4 reports 26.39% reversed and 26.63% randomized versus 27.06% normal order. Table 1 revises ActAlign from 30.29 to 30.40±0.11, and the abstract changes 30.5% to 30.4%, while retained ablations still report 30.29%.

T1.justification: The mathematical definitions, DTW constraints and recurrence, normalization and prediction rules remain substantively unchanged. Appendix B.4 repeats the O(NMT) complexity already stated in v2 Section 4.1 and adds discussion rather than a new formal result or proof.

C1.justification: Both retain the central claims of training-free, model-agnostic and domain-general recognition through language-guided DTW, outperforming the reported ActionAtlas baselines without video–text supervision. The contribution list and conclusion are not substantively redefined.

C2.justification: V3 adds scalability and parallelization arguments in Appendix B.4 and interprets the domain breakdown as consistent improvement. The new domain-improvement wording overlooks a cheerleading Top-1 tie and a wrestling Top-3 loss in Table 10. Existing ambiguity and global-alignment limitations remain.

D1.justification: V3 specifies the metadata source of sport names and pretrained origin of SigLIP scaling parameters, and adds VLM preprocessing, frame and token details in Appendix H/Table 12. The listed code pointer changes from a repository to a project page. Conversely, the T=0.2 setting in v2 Table 4's caption is omitted from corresponding v3 Table 6.

R1.justification: V3 removes Mahjourian and Nguyen (2025), Sanitizing Manufacturing Dataset Labels Using Vision-Language Models, from the image-language discussion and bibliography. The remaining research positioning is substantially retained; expanded bibliographic formatting does not constitute new related work.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and section ordering are retained. V3 makes limited explanatory and terminology edits, numbers additional subsections, and updates author/contact and publication-header text. Added experimental passages and appendices do not amount to a wholesale narrative rewrite.

P2.justification: V3 converts the two-column main text to a single-column journal layout, substantially resizing and relocating retained displays. It adds Tables 3–4 and 10–12 plus Figure 9; the original prompting, script and statistics tables remain under new numbering.

improvement.justification: The stronger pooling controls and order-perturbation tests make the central alignment contribution easier to assess, while domain results and VLM settings improve transparency. These gains are limited by modest order effects that receive little interpretation, overbroad domain-improvement wording, and an unexplained relationship between the revised 30.40±0.11 main result and retained 30.29 entries.
